songInfo.title: Learn to Fly
songInfo.album: There Is Nothing Left to Lose

scalesUsed.application: The bright, uplifting scale governing the soaring power chords and vocal melody
Supplies the catchy melodic lead guitar counter-melodies in the verses and bridge

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Uplifting, sunlit alternative rock anthem combining chiming open string voicings (Bsus4, E) with power pop drive and modal borrowed chords
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: G# minor is the relative minor

mainProgression.progression: I - v - IV | I - vi - IV | ♭VI - ♭VII - I
mainProgression.progressionDescription: Chiming B major verse with borrowed minor v chord (F#m), moving into a triumphant chorus and chromatic rock bridge.
mainProgression.description: Chiming B major verse with borrowed minor v chord (F#m), moving into a triumphant chorus and chromatic rock bridge.

sectionProgressions.description: Ringing Bsus4 and open E voicings with the borrowed minor v chord providing wistful alternative color
Full overdriven power chords under 'Looking to the sky to save me'
Classic rock double-step chromatic ascent driving into the final chorus explosion

harmonicFunction: B (I) - Bright, uplifting rock tonic with open high B and E string chime
F#m (v) - Borrowed minor dominant chord introducing poignant melancholic contrast
E (IV) - Major subdominant delivering warm resolution and lift
G#m (vi) - Relative minor adding emotional depth in the chorus
G (♭VI) & A (♭VII) - Chromatic modal rock cadence propelling the bridge climax

techniques.name: Open-String Chime Voicings & Driving Eighth-Note Rhythm
techniques.description: Fretting modified barre chord roots on the 5th and 6th strings while leaving strings 1 and 2 open to ring as shimmering drone tones

notes: B chord: 7-9-9-8-0-0 or X-2-4-4-0-0 (Bsus4/Badd9 flavor with ringing open high B and E)
F#m chord: 2-4-4-2-0-0 (ringing open high strings)
E chord: 0-2-2-1-0-0 (full open E major)
sequence: Fret the B shape and strum in steady eighth notes at 136 BPM
Shift cleanly to F#m, keeping the high strings open
Resolve to full open E major on beat 1
Swell into full distortion for the chorus
tips: Let strings 1 and 2 ring across ALL chord changes—this is the sonic glue of the Foo Fighters guitar sound
Recorded at Dave Grohl's home studio in Virginia using Vox AC30 and Mesa Dual Rectifier combinations
Keep your right wrist relaxed for the driving 136 BPM tempo

techniques.name: Chromatic Modal Bridge Ascent & Chris Shiflett Melodic Lead Fills
techniques.description: Executing Chris Shiflett's bright major pentatonic lead counterpoint on the high B and E strings while transitioning into the chromatic G - A - B bridge build

notes: Lead fill on strings 1 and 2: 7th and 9th frets (F#, G#, B, C#)
Chromatic bridge power chords: G5 (3-5-5-X-X-X) to A5 (5-7-7-X-X-X) resolving triumphantly to B5 (7-9-9-X-X-X)
Targeting chord tones: D# over the B chord, F# over F#m, and G# over E
sequence: Pick cleanly across strings 1 and 2 using alternate picking
Accent the rhythmic syncopation on beats 2 and 4
Shift up horizontally for the G5 → A5 → B5 bridge crescendo
Let the open strings ring as the final chorus explodes
tips: Use a Stratocaster bridge or middle pickup for bite that cuts through Grohl's heavy rhythm wall
Don't rush the chromatic power chord shifts—lock squarely with Taylor Hawkins' snare
Hold the pick firmly for lead attack but keep the wrist loose

sections.name: Intro Chiming Verse Progression
sections.description: Dave Grohl and Chris Shiflett's ringing clean-to-crunch verse progression.
notes: Let open high E and B strings ring continuously
Notice the borrowed F#m chord
Steady, driving eighth-note strumming

sections.name: Verse 1 Ringing Open Drones
sections.description: The driving verse groove under Grohl's melodic opening lyrics ('Run and tell all of the angels').
notes: Keep the Bsus4 shape anchored on strings 3 and 4
Allow strings 1 and 2 to ring as stationary drones
Build dynamic intensity heading into the chorus

sections.name: Chorus 1 Stadium Power Chords
sections.description: Massive distorted chorus 'Looking to the sky to save me, looking for a sign of life'.
notes: Heavy downstroke power chords
Accentuate beats 2 and 4
Lock tight with Taylor Hawkins' driving drum beat

sections.name: Verse 2 Shiflett Melodic Lead Counterpoint
sections.description: Chris Shiflett's bright lead guitar counter-melody dancing over the rhythm in the second verse.
notes: Clean alternate picking on strings 1 and 2
Bright, singing Stratocaster bridge pickup tone
Target chord tones (D# on B, F# on F#m)

sections.name: Bridge Chromatic Double-Step Ascent
sections.description: The dynamic bridge climb moving from flat-six (G) up through flat-seven (A) to the home B tonic.
notes: Full unmuted power chords with heavy overdrive
Driving straight eighth notes
Crescendo into the explosive final chorus

sections.name: Chorus 2 & Final Ringing Cadence
sections.description: Triumphant double chorus with all guitar layers blazing, ending on a ringing open B chord.
notes: Wide open power chord downstrokes
Sustain the final B major chord into feedback
Let the ringing open B and high E strings ring out

guitar.recommended: Gibson DG-335 or Gibson Les Paul Standard
guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker for crunchy rhythm; Neck for clean intro warmth

amp.recommended: Vox AC30 Top Boost blended with Mesa/Boogie Dual Rectifier

effects.distortion: ProCo Rat 2 or Boss DS-1 (for chorus boost)

beginner.title: Chorus Chords & Strumming
steps: Learn the B, G#m, and E power chords
Practice steady eighth-note downstrokes at 110 BPM

intermediate.title: Open-String Verse Chords
steps: Master the Bsus4 and F#m open-string chord voicings
Transition smoothly between B, F#m, and E at 136 BPM
Learn the chromatic bridge progression (G → A → B)

advanced.title: Lead Counterpoint & Dynamics
steps: Learn Chris Shiflett's melodic lead fills note-for-note
Coordinate dual-guitar interplay between clean chime and heavy crunch
Perform with authentic arena rock energy and vocal support

commonMistakes: Muting the high open strings during the verse B and F#m chord shapes
Rushing the tempo during the chorus explosion
Fumbling the chromatic bridge chord transitions (G → A → B)
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Open-string chord voicings isolation (B → F#m → E)
5 minutes: Chorus power chord strumming with metronome at 136 BPM
5 minutes: Bridge chromatic climb (G → A → B)
focusAreas: Dynamic shift from verse to chorus
metronomeWork: Practice at 115 BPM to lock in chord changes, then advance to 136 BPM
